title: Cloudflare Reclaims 100 TB of RAM by Optimizing Consistent Hashing
gist: Cloudflare cut more than 100 TB of memory from its Pingora Backend Router by optimizing the pingora-ketama consistent-hashing library in Rust. Probability analysis let it use about 90% fewer hashes per backend without losing distribution accuracy, and hash-ring entries were compacted from 8 to 6 bytes. The new ring was rolled out gradually so the change did not invalidate the cache and spike origin traffic.

insights.claim: Cloudflare reduced the memory footprint of its internal load-balancing service by more than 100 TB by optimizing the Rust consistent-hashing implementation in pingora-ketama. Hash-ring entries were compacted and the number of hashes per backend fell by about 90% while load-balancing accuracy was preserved.

insights.so_what: Software efficiency gains at hyperscale lower Cloudflare's capex and memory needs, which helps gross margins during a period of high DRAM prices.

insights.claim: Cloudflare engineers found that each step down in load-distribution error margin requires roughly an order of magnitude more hashes per server, so adding hashes gives sharply diminishing returns. The final 90,000 hashes improved error by only 0.7%.
